subject: [PATCH v4 1/3] mm: swap: move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator

2026-09-11.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a new folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator function. This change is necessary to allow callers of the allocator function to act on the newly allocated folio before it becomes visible for reclaim. The patch also addresses issues related to refault evaluation and zswap writeback dropbehind, where the buffer folio needs to stay off the LRU entirely. The functional changes are minimal, as each caller will add the folio to the LRU after allocation.

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Kairui Song pointed out that the comment about swap_cache_alloc_folio() adding a folio to the LRU itself was incorrect, as it is actually __swap_cache_alloc_folio() that has been renamed in this patch.

Gave Reviewed-by
reviews.raw_body:
I think you mean:
"swap_cache_alloc_folio() adds the new folio to the LRU itself"

__swap_cache_alloc_folio is the new name you introduced in this patch.

2026-09-14.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a new folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator function. The current implementation adds the folio to the LRU immediately, which prevents callers from acting on the folio before it becomes visible for reclaim. This change is necessary for two use cases: refault evaluation and zswap writeback dropbehind. By deferring the LRU insertion to the callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(), there is no functional change intended, but rather a preparatory step for future changes.

reviews.author: Alexandre Ghiti
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti noted that the patch does not address the issue of swap cache folios being added to the LRU before they are fully initialized, which can lead to incorrect behavior in certain scenarios.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti thanked the patch submitter without raising any specific technical concerns or objections.
